public_payload.normalized_proposition: Meta does not really have an AI business despite its AI capex.

statement.excerpt: As I’ve hinted at, Meta is in the same boat, except far worse, because it doesn’t really have an AI business.

from_speaker: doesn’t really have an AI business
in the same boat, except far worse
our_interpretation: Read 'AI business' as a substantive commercial activity selling AI products or services to customers, beyond using AI internally to improve advertising.
AI-enabled consumer products are relevant; they are not automatically excluded merely because they include hardware.
The word 'really' suggests commercial substance, but supplies no revenue or materiality threshold.
Use April through June 2026, the latest completed quarterly reporting period before the September 1 post, for the ongoing observation.
Later announcements are context unless they explicitly establish activity during that quarter.
This is a claim about the existence and substance of a business, not a claim of a specified revenue amount. The relative judgment 'far worse' has no supplied comparison measure.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous product and financial records establish that Meta had no substantive customer-facing AI commercial activity during the target quarter, with AI monetization confined to indirect improvements in its existing advertising business.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous records establish substantive sales of AI products or services during the target quarter. A product announcement or an unquantified minor revenue stream alone does not settle the qualifier 'really.'
